 Dayton is 5-4 in three appearances at South Carolina event

 David Jablonski 
 The Flyer Faithful began filing out of UD Arena early in a 95-72 loss to the Cincinnati Bearcats on Saturday, Nov. 14. They didn’t stick around to witness the end of another disappointing game.
 Three days later, Dayton Flyers fans left early for the traditional reason — to beat the traffic.
 Dayton coasted to an 88-63 victory against Central Michigan on Tuesday, Nov. 17, ending a three-game home losing streak just in time to build some confidence for their first games away from home at the Charleston Classic.
 “I just tell my guys to stay the course,” Dayton forward Jalen Haynes said. “I feel like media and everybody, they just get caught up in the names and the transfers that we have, but they don’t know stuff like this is supposed to happen. We have a young team. We’re going to make mistakes. We’ve just got to get used to winning. I tell them, ‘Keep building winning habits and keep doing the right things, and good things are gonna happen.’”
 Good things happened the last time Dayton traveled to Charleston, S.C., in November 2023. The Flyers beat LSU and St. John’s before losing to Houston in the championship game. Those two victories helped Dayton earn an NCAA tournament at-large bid that season.
 The Flyers will make their fourth appearance in the event and third during coach Anthony Grant’s 10-year tenure this weekend. They play Utah (3-1) at 5:30 p.m. Friday, Nov. 20, and Northwestern (3-2) at 1 p.m. Sunday, Nov. 22.
 The Shriners Charleston Classic no longer uses a traditional tournament format. Dayton knows its two opponents ahead of time. For the second straight season in a November event, Dayton will play only two games instead of the traditional three. 
 RELATED: Walk-on tradition continues with senior trio The event starts at 12:30 p.m. Friday with a game between Oklahoma State and Minnesota. Northwestern plays Virginia Tech in the second game at 3 p.m.
 “I’m appreciative of Shriners being our sponsor,” Grant said. “We had a chance to meet a young man and his mom who’s a beneficiary of what Shriners Hospital does, and so for our guys to get to know a little bit more about that and to see the impact that it has on families, I’m grateful for that.
 “Charleston’s a great location. The College of Charleston’s gym is a hooper’s gym, so to speak. It’s a great atmosphere there. It’s got a great feel to it. It’s going to be a really good field. It’s very competitive.”
 Here are five things to know about the Utah matchup:
 1: Series history 
 The series is tied 1-1. The teams haven’t met in 68 years.
 The Flyers beat Utah 77-73 at Kentucky’s Memorial Coliseum on Dec. 20, 1955.
 Utah beat Dayton 79-70 at Madison Square Garden on Dec. 29, 1958.
 Dayton has lost five straight games against Big 12 opponents. Three of those losses have come against Cincinnati.
 The Flyers are 2-8 against the Big 12 in Grant’s tenure with victories against Cincinnati in 2023 and Kansas in 2021.
 Utah head coach Alex Jensen talks to his players during the first half of an NCAA college basketball game against Cincinnati at the Big 12 Conference tournament, March 10, 2026, in Kansas City, Mo. AP Photo/Charlie Riedel
 AP Photo/Charlie Riedel 
 2: State of the program 
 Utah finished 10-22 last season — coach Alex Jensen’s first season. He replaced Craig Smith (65-62 in four seasons).
 Jensen was Utah’s Mr. Basketball in 1994 and played for the Utah team that reached the national championship game under Rick Majerus in 1998.
 Jensen coached against Dayton as an assistant for Majerus at Saint Louis from 2007-11.
 Utah has four losing seasons and one 20-win season in the last eight years. It last played in the NCAA tournament in 2016. From 1991-2005, it played in the NCAA tournament 12 times in 15 seasons.
 Utah was picked to finish last in the Big 12 preseason poll.
 3: Scouting report 
 Utah lost its top eight scorers, including guard Terrence Brown (19.9 points per game), who transferred to North Carolina.
 Alec Anigbata, a 6-foot-9 freshman forward, leads Utah with 15.0 points per game.
 Trey Campbell, a 6-4 fifth-year guard, ranks second in scoring with 14.2 points per game. He scored 1,403 points in four seasons at Northern Iowa.
 Jackson Holcombe, a 6-6, fourth-year guard, is Utah’s other double-digit scorer (13.2). He spent the last three seasons at Utah Valley.
 Two of Utah’s five new transfers have Ohio connections. Former Wright State guard TJ Burch has started three games, averaging 6.5 points. Former Ohio State guard Taison Chatman averages 7.2 points.
 4: Season summary Utah opened the season with three victories, beating Long Beach State 66-63, Towson 67-57 and Weber State 85-64.
 On Tuesday, Utah lost 71-67 at home to Eastern Washington (2-3). Utah shot 18.8% (6 of 32) from 3-point range.
 Jensen said, “We’ve got to get a lot better. I told the guys, ‘It kind of seems like we’ve been playing like we’ve accomplished something, and we’re far from it.’ We’ll watch film. We might change the rotation somewhat, but we’ve got to come out at the start of the game like we do in the second half.”
 Dayton’s Jalen Haynes, right, slaps hands with Tristian Ford after scoring against Central Michigan on Tuesday, Nov. 17, 2026, at UD Arena. David Jablonski
 David Jablonski 
 5: Odds & Ends KenPom.com gives Dayton a 47% chance of winning and predicts a 72-71 score. Dayton climbed from No. 124 to No. 114 in the Ken Pomeroy ratings after beating Central Michigan. Utah fell from No. 95 to No. 104 after losing to Eastern Washington.
 Haynes reached the 1,000-point milestone Tuesday in his fourth college season on the court. He has 1,003 points in 81 games.
 Dayton is 5-4 in three appearances at the Charleston Classic. It is 11-12 in November tournaments during Grant’s tenure.
